items.headline: Wind Advisory issued October 16 at 1:15AM EDT until October 17 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
items.description:
* WHAT...North winds 10 to 20 mph with gusts up to 35 mph expected.

* WHERE...Portions of southeast Alabama and Big Bend and Panhandle
Florida.

* WHEN...From midnight tonight to 7 PM CDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Strong gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects and
compromised trees. Trees damaged from Hurricane Isaias will be
extra vulnerable to the elevated winds that may result in more
downed trees in the area. In addition, large debris piles from
storm cleanup may be blown about resulting in additional hazards to
anyone nearby outdoors. Tree limbs could be blown down and a few
power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Frequent wind gusts forecast around 30-35 mph
will create dangerous conditions outdoors in the vulnerable areas.
Elsewhere, winds may result in large tree branches downed and
localized power outages.
items.instruction:
Winds this strong can make driving difficult, especially for high
profile vehicles. Use extra caution.

Secure outdoor objects.

Remain alert for potential falling trees and power lines, blown
debris, and additional damage to structures that remain compromised
from the hurricane.

items.headline: Gale Warning issued October 16 at 2:55AM EDT until October 18 at 8:00AM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
items.description:
* WHAT...North winds 20 to 30 kt with gusts up to 40 kt and seas
6 to 9 ft expected.

* WHERE...Offshore Gulf waters from the Walton-Okaloosa County
line to Apalachicola from 20 to 60 nautical miles out, Coastal
waters from Mexico Beach to Okaloosa Walton County Line FL out
20 NM, and Coastal waters from Mexico Beach to Apalachicola FL
out 20 NM.

* WHEN...From 7 PM this evening to 7 AM CDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Strong winds will cause hazardous seas which could
capsize or damage vessels and reduce visibility.
items.instruction:
Mariners should alter plans to avoid these hazardous conditions.
Remain in port, seek safe harbor, alter course, and/or secure the
vessel for severe conditions.
